title: `go fmt` and `goimports`: formatting that ends the argument

videos.script: Almost every Go file you open looks the same. Same tabs, same spacing, same braces. Nobody had to agree on that. One program does it, and this lesson is about that program. {{gofmt}} First, gofmt. You give it an untidy file, and it prints the file back in the one layout Go has. Three flags decide where the result goes: a list of files, a diff, or the file rewritten. And go fmt is the same program, run over your packages. {{decides}} Then what it decides, and what it leaves to you. It has no settings at all, and that ends an argument every team has. It never wraps a long line, and it never renames anything. {{imports}} Next, goimports. It formats like gofmt, and it also writes your import block. It adds what you use, removes what you do not, and puts your own packages in a group of their own. {{pipeline}} Last, the check that runs before a commit and in CI. Its first version is usually wrong, because gofmt reports success while listing unformatted files. You will see that happen, and then a check that fails when it should.
